title: Resolucao dinamica de modelos por backend (codex + claude): descobrir/validar slugs em vez de pinar
description: PROBLEMA: hoje pinamos slugs de modelo concretos na config (project.toml [models], e para codex [models.codex].<phase>). Slug concreto apodrece: gpt-5.3-codex foi aposentado pela OpenAI e virou HTTP 400 'not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account', MAL-DIAGNOSTICADO como wall de entitlement de conta bloqueando CAM-54 (journal SESSION-CAM396/CAM-397 2026-07-22). Causa real: slug morto na config, nao entitlement. Conta ChatGPT Plus usa codex normalmente com slugs atuais (validado ao vivo: gpt-5.6-sol/gpt-5.5/codex-auto-review respondem via `codex exec`; gpt-5.3-codex/gpt-5.1-codex/gpt-5/o3 todos 400). OBJETIVO: camada de resolucao/validacao de modelo que descobre a lista de slugs disponiveis por backend e valida ou auto-resolve o modelo configurado antes do dispatch. CODEX: ler ~/.codex/models_cache.json (mantido pelo codex; campos slug/display_name/visibility/supported_in_api/priority). Politica deterministica: filtrar visibility=='list' && supported_in_api==true, ordenar por priority asc, pegar topo (hoje gpt-5.6-sol, priority 1). Slug pinado vira override opcional; fallback pro pinado se parse falhar. FRAGILIDADE (fator de custo, nao rebaixa a recomendacao): models_cache.json e cache interno nao-documentado do codex, schema pode mudar entre versoes, nao existe `codex models` publico (codex-cli 0.144.6). Precisa fallback + parse resiliente. CLAUDE: sem apodrecimento hoje (opus/sonnet sao aliases publicos estaveis resolvidos server-side), mas o operador quer descoberta/validacao consistente pros dois backends. FORK PRA GRILLING/SPEC: como enumerar modelos claude na CLI de subscription (sem API key, projeto subscription-only)? existe `claude models`? No minimo validar/fail-closed com aviso se o modelo configurado nao resolver, em vez de 400 silencioso. TOUCH POINTS: readNestedBackendModel (sem claude-alias guard: sem [models.codex].<phase> o codex recebe alias claude flat tipo 'opus'), readPhaseModel, src/supervisor/backend-adapter.ts, camada de config. TIPO feat. Precisa grilling/spec antes de build (fork claude-enumeration + fragilidade cache interno). Relacionado CAM-54. Interino: CAM-54 fecha com gpt-5.6-sol pinado.

spec.scope: Add a dynamic model-resolution and validation layer that runs at model-resolution time, before every LLM dispatch. CODEX: honor a nested [models.codex].<phase> slug as the highest-precedence pin; ALSO honor a non-empty, non-claude-shaped flat [models].<phase> value as a valid codex pin (this preserves configurations that dispatch fine on main today, including the repo's own gpt-5-codex fixtures); when no valid pin exists, auto-resolve from ~/.codex/models_cache.json (filter visibility==list AND supported_in_api==true, sort priority ascending, pick top); fail closed with an actionable error only when there is no valid pin AND the cache is missing/unreadable/schema-incompatible, instead of leaking a claude alias into `codex exec -m`. CLAUDE: a deterministic typo-guard that fails closed with a warning when the configured model is neither a known alias (default, best, fable, opus, sonnet, haiku, opusplan, sonnet[1m], opus[1m]) nor a claude-* full-name. INTEGRATION POINT: plug the layer at the existing readPhaseModel call site at each of the five dispatch sites; do NOT move codexAuthPreflight or reorder it relative to buildSpawnArgv. OUT OF SCOPE: any live probing of claude models (impossible under subscription-only: no `claude models` command, /model is interactive-picker-only, subscription OAuth cannot hit /v1/models); any API-key-based enumeration; any change to src/ui/ConfigScreen.tsx (deriving MODEL_OPTIONS or adding a picker warning is not traceable to this issue's acceptance criteria); and the pre-existing orchestrator-codex dispatch gap (buildOrchestratorPaneCommand hardcodes claude at run.ts:275).
acceptanceCriteria: For the codex backend, when neither a nested `[models.codex].<phase>` pin nor a non-claude-shaped flat `[models].<phase>` value is configured, the model dispatched to `codex exec -m` is auto-resolved from `~/.codex/models_cache.json` (entries filtered to visibility==list and supported_in_api==true, sorted by priority ascending, top slug chosen); it never falls through to a claude alias. [oracle: reviewer-judgment]

A nested `[models.codex].<phase>` slug is honored verbatim as the highest-precedence pin, and a non-empty non-claude-shaped flat `[models].<phase>` value is ALSO honored as a valid codex pin, preserving configurations that dispatch fine on main today (including the repo's own gpt-5-codex fixtures); neither is replaced by cache auto-resolution. [oracle: reviewer-judgment]

When the codex cache is missing, unreadable, or schema-incompatible AND no valid pin (nested or flat) exists, the codex dispatch fails closed at model-resolution time with an actionable error naming the cache path and the pin remedy; no codex exec process is spawned with an unresolved or claude-alias model. [oracle: reviewer-judgment]

For the claude backend, a configured model that is neither a known alias (default, best, fable, opus, sonnet, haiku, opusplan, sonnet[1m], opus[1m]) nor a claude-* full-name causes the dispatch to fail closed with a warning naming the offending value; any valid alias or claude-* full-name proceeds unchanged. [oracle: reviewer-judgment]

The resolution and validation layer is invoked at the existing model-resolution call site where readPhaseModel is already called at each of the five dispatch sites, which measurably precedes argv-build at every site; no control-flow reorder of codexAuthPreflight relative to buildSpawnArgv is performed, and the pre-existing container ensure and preflight early-return ordering assertions continue to hold. [oracle: reviewer-judgment]

The codex models-cache reader is a pure function behind an injectable DI seam mirroring codexAuthCheck in src/supervisor/codex-auth.ts, unit-tested with fakes for the list/supported/priority filter and the fail-closed empty and malformed paths, with the real default reader covered by a scratch-tmpdir test that does not monkeypatch os.homedir(). [oracle: reviewer-judgment]

CONTEXT.md's tier-alias term is updated to the full current alias set including best, and docs/recovery-runbook.md gains an entry for the new operator-facing fail-closed abort naming the codex models cache path. [oracle: reviewer-judgment]
The model-config resolution test suite passes, including the extended backend-aware resolution, flat-pin precedence and claude typo-guard cases. [oracle: bun test test/config/models.test.ts]
The full quality spine passes. [oracle: bun run check:all]
gotchas: MEASURED ORDERING (a previous spec revision got this wrong; trust these numbers, they were verified live on main): the spawn argv is built BEFORE codexAuthPreflight at THREE of the five sites: loop.ts builds at :1113 while preflight runs at :1238 (with ensureWorkerPane, the @cam_label set-option, clearWorkerReport, ensureContainerFn and preflightContainerFn early-returns, and dockerExecWrap in between); review.ts builds shellCmd at :386 and dispatchCmd at :428 while preflight runs at :443; run.ts builds via buildOrchestratorPaneCommand at :460 while preflight runs at :495. Only the two plan-runner.ts sites are preflight-then-build (:633 -> :643 and :690 -> :700). Therefore do NOT design around 'preflight runs immediately before argv-build'.

BECAUSE of the ordering above, plug the resolution/validation layer at the readPhaseModel call site, NOT at the codexAuthPreflight choke. readPhaseModel is called at loop.ts:1095, review.ts:379, plan-runner.ts:629 and :686, run.ts:458, and each of those measurably precedes that site's argv-build, so resolving and failing closed there needs ZERO control-flow reorder and does not disturb the container ensure/preflight early-returns that existing loop tests assert.

FLAT-PIN POLICY (decided, do not re-litigate): a non-empty, non-claude-shaped flat [models].<phase> value IS a valid codex pin. Three of the repo's own fixtures rely on exactly that shape (loop.test.ts:528 and :4236, plan-runner-codex-auth.test.ts:111, run-codex-auth.test.ts:112, all 'gpt-5-codex'), and hosts or CI machines that have never run codex have no ~/.codex/models_cache.json at all. Treating flat values as invalid would turn configurations that dispatch fine on main into hard aborts and force an operator migration. Do NOT rewrite those fixtures to the nested table.

A partial guard already exists downstream at codexAuthPreflight + isClaudeAliasModel (src/supervisor/codex-auth.ts:77,127); its regex /\b(opus|sonnet|haiku)\b/i misses default/fable/opusplan/sonnet[1m]/opus[1m]. Reuse or extend that claude-shape predicate as the 'is this flat value a claude alias' test rather than adding a second divergent notion of claude-shaped.

readPhaseModel fallback chain (src/config/models.ts:158-178): [models.<backend>].<phase> (skipped when backend is undefined or claude) -> flat [models].<phase> -> DEFAULTS[phase]. test/config/models.test.ts:265-291 currently asserts the codex-falls-to-flat behavior as intentional; under the decided flat-pin policy that assertion largely STAYS valid (a non-claude flat value is still honored) and only the claude-alias-flat case changes.

No codex models_cache reader exists anywhere (grep models_cache = 0 hits in src and test). The only ~/.codex/* code today is codexAuthCheck reading ~/.codex/auth.json via existsSync (src/supervisor/codex-auth.ts:60). Mirror its DI-seam idiom: an injectable reader fn for fakes plus a separate scratch-tmpdir test of the real reader; never monkeypatch os.homedir().

models_cache.json is an undocumented internal codex cache; schema is { models: [ { slug, display_name, visibility, supported_in_api, priority, ... } ] } and codex-cli 0.144.6 has no public `codex models`. Parse resiliently; on schema drift fall back to the pin, and fail closed only when there is also no pin. This fragility is a cost factor, not a reason to weaken fail-closed.

The claude alias list to reuse is MODEL_OPTIONS in src/ui/ConfigScreen.tsx:98-107 (8 entries; it omits `best`). Read it or relocate the canonical list to a non-UI module, but do NOT change the picker UI or add a picker warning: that is explicitly out of scope.

loop.ts and plan-runner.ts have NO configPath test seam (only review.ts does, via MakeReviewDispatchOptions.configPath from CAM-405). Their tests chdir into a tmpdir with a staged scripts/cam/project.toml (loop.test.ts withCodexBackendCwd helper). Follow that precedent; do not add a configPath seam to loop/plan-runner unless a story specifically needs it.
If an ADR is warranted, the next free number is 0049: docs/adr/0041 through 0048 already exist on main (0041 is the operator-decision-gates ADR).

ship is deterministic/zero-LLM (ADR-0009) with no dispatch site, so there is no 6th call site. The orchestrator resolves and gates codex but buildOrchestratorPaneCommand hardcodes claude (run.ts:275); leave that pre-existing gap out of scope.
domainTerms: model resolution: turning a configured phase+backend into the concrete model slug passed to the spawned LLM process (codex exec -m / claude --model), including cache auto-resolution for codex.

pin: an operator-configured concrete model slug that overrides auto-resolution; for codex a pin may come from the nested [models.codex].<phase> key (highest precedence) or from a non-claude-shaped flat [models].<phase> value.
typo-guard: a deterministic fail-closed validation that a configured claude model is a known alias or a claude-* full-name, catching project.toml misconfiguration before dispatch.
models_cache.json: codex's undocumented internal cache at ~/.codex/models_cache.json listing available model slugs with visibility/supported_in_api/priority fields.
